topic: Someone receives flowers with no card attached
text: The rain wasn't letting up, but that's not why I was hunched over the desk, fingers drumming a steady rhythm on the chipped wooden surface. The phone gave a solitary ring—a sound that's rare enough to turn your blood cold these days. I picked it up, my voice steady. "Spenshere." The line buzzed with static for a moment before a clipped, nervous voice cut through. "Mr. Spenshere, I... received some flowers. No card. Thought it might be... something." I leaned back, the creak of the old leather chair a familiar comfort. "Flowers, huh? No sender, no note. Could be a admirer, or could be a warning. You said ‘something’—what's that supposed to mean?" The pause on the other end stretched long. "Just a feeling, I suppose." "Feelings are one thing, facts are another. I'll see what I can dig up. spills start with a drop." I hung up, the weight of the phone heavy in my hand. Something was off, and that usually meant the rain was about to get a lot heavier.
